simple.meaning: צָחַק (tsâchaq) is a Hebrew concept word meaning “to laugh outright (in merriment or scorn); by implication, to sport.” BibleIQ follows how Scripture develops this idea across its occurrences.
simple.biblicalBackground: The concept appears 13 times across Genesis, Exodus, Judges, beginning at Genesis 17:17. Its contexts include birth, family line, Torah, city.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to צָחַק (H6711).
simple.whyItMatters: Concept words shape biblical themes. BibleIQ keeps the concept grounded in actual verse evidence instead of starting with a later theological definition.
simple.summary: צָחַק (tsâchaq) / H6711 is traced through Genesis 17:17, Genesis 18:12, Genesis 18:13, Genesis 18:15 as a generated source-based concept entry.

timeline.evidenceText: Then Abraham fell on his face, and laughed, and said in his heart, “Will a child be born to him who is one hundred years old? Will Sarah, who is ninety years old, give birth?”
Sarah laughed within herself, saying, “After I have grown old will I have pleasure, my lord being old also?”
Yahweh said to Abraham, “Why did Sarah laugh, saying, ‘Will I really bear a child when I am old?’
Then Sarah denied it, saying, “I didn’t laugh,” for she was afraid.

Lot went out, and spoke to his sons-in-law, who were pledged to marry his daughters, and said, “Get up! Get out of this place, for Yahweh will destroy the city!”
Sarah said, “God has made me laugh. Everyone who hears will laugh with me.”
Sarah saw the son of Hagar the Egyptian, whom she had borne to Abraham, mocking.
When he had been there a long time, Abimelech king of the Philistines looked out at a window, and saw, and, behold, Isaac was caressing Rebekah, his wife.

Pi`el Imperfect וַיְצַחֵק Judg 16:25 ; Infinitive construct לְצַחֵק Exod 32:6 , (בִּיׅ בָּנוּ לְצַ֫חֶק Gen 39:14 , 17 ; Participle מְצַחֵק 19:14 ; 26:8 , מְצַחֶ֑ק 21:9 ; — 1 jest Gen 19:14 (J). 2 sport, play Gen 21:9 (E) Exod 32:6 (J); make sport for Judg 16:25 ( לִפְנֵי ; || וִישַׂחֶקלָֿ֑נוּ ); toy with ( אֶת ), of conjugal caresses Gen 26:8 (compare Doughty Arab.
